newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Czech President Havel sees more trade in Argentina.
newsitem.headline: Czech President Havel sees more trade in Argentina.

text.p: Czech Republic President Vaclav Havel praised Friday Argentina's economic reforms and said President Carlos Menem's outward-looking policies are helping promote investment and trade between both countries.

"Menem's personality and his commitment to democracy are well known," Havel told a news conference on his second day of a three-day official visit to Argentina. "And his aggressive opening to the world is helping investments."

Pushed to specify which sectors could benefit from increased trade, Havel said that it was not the government's job to decide where and what to invest. Rather that of private buisnessmen, such as the forty entrepreneurs accompanying him on his Latin American trip.
"But my government is a liberal one and we are doing every effort to eliminate obstacles to trade," he said.

An aide to Havel said that apart from a specific proposal to invest in Argentina by Czech carmaker Skoda, he believed opportunities could arise in construction, energy and building equipment, among others.
"Even the famous beer company Pilsner could one day produce in Argentina," he said with a smile.
Menem praised Havel for his achievements as a writer, an intellectual and a man who fought for democracy.
The Czech leader began a Latin American tour September 16 in Brazil, where he spent a week. He also travelled to Chile and Uruguay before arriving in Argentina last Thursday.
Before heading back to Prague, he will briefly return to Brazil Saturday for some sight-seeing at the Foz de Iguacu waterfalls.
